newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence falls in June qtr -NZIER.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence falls in June qtr -NZIER.

text.p: New Zealand business confidence fell again in the June quarter, although on a seasonally adjusted basis the fall was not as severe as in the March quarter, the NZIER said in releasing its Quarterly Survey of Economic Opinion on Thursday.

Confidence fell in most sectors, with the exception of financial service firms, which reported a rise in confidence. Financial sector firms were now optimistic and expected the business situation to improve.

"Manufacturing firms are the most pessimistic, and appear to be going through an unprecendented deflationary period," NZIER said. "They reported a sharp fall in prices, with the decline being the largest ever recorded in the NZIER survey."
There were, however, a few rays of hope. Manufacturers expected export sales to increase next quarter, which NZIER said may reflect an easing exchange rate.

Furthermore, Australian manufacturers were increasingly confident about their domestic economy. "This is good news for our manufacturers, since Australia is still the main destination for our manufactured exports."
NZIER said business pessimism -- the converse of business confidence -- and the Reserve Bank's recently constructed real Monetary Conditions Index (real MCI) track together reasonably closely.
"But given that monetary policy will only ease slightly over the rest of 1997, something else may be needed to push up business confidence," the Institute said.
"In the absence of the 1997 tax cut, that 'something else' could be additional government spending."
NZIER said the results of the survey confirmed that economic growth was likely to stay low for some quarters yet.
